title: Field Report: Exorcist 98 on public MCP servers and agent-config repositories

precision.note: Round 2: a fresh held-out set scanned once with the fixed rules. Of 34 high or critical issues, 0 were real and 5 debatable (47 findings: 0 real, 9 debatable).

notableDebatable.title: Encoded payload
notableDebatable.label: debatable
notableDebatable.description: An MCP server stores Windows process-memory API signatures (OpenProcess, ReadProcessMemory, WriteProcessMemory) as base64 in a file named obfuscated-strings.ts. Not instructions to an AI, but deliberately hidden from anyone reading the source.

notableDebatable.title: Remote code in hook
notableDebatable.label: debatable
notableDebatable.description: The dev container pipes the official uv installer into sh every time the environment is created. Real fetch-and-run inside the agent environment, from an official source.

notableDebatable.title: Secrets in agent reach
notableDebatable.label: debatable
notableDebatable.description: A value in Google API key format sits in an evaluation case for a guard. Probably synthetic test data; we did not test it and do not reproduce it.

falsePositivePatterns.description: Attack samples kept as test data or saved benchmark results of a defence (labelled "malicious", "blocked": true).
Base64 certificates and public keys (kubeconfigs in saved test output, release-signing keys).
Bidi characters inside code that strips them, quoted in a plan document.
HTML comments written for people (template hints, metadata, maintainer notes) that name an AI product or mention exfiltration but give the AI no order.
Example payloads listed in prompt-injection testing guides, plain and base64-encoded.
Install commands listed as data or documentation, which nothing runs as a hook.
Copied vendor documentation that warns against, or describes, bypassing safety checks.
Risk notes saying that something "could bypass safety checks".

round1.note: Round 1: a different held-out set, scanned with the rules before these fixes. Kept here for honesty.

round1DevRerun.note: The round-1 repositories scanned again with the fixed rules. The fixes were designed by looking at these repositories, so this is a development set, not a measure of precision.
